question: I am extending the candidate-source seam from video to image collections. What existing contracts and image-specific behavior should the implementation retain?
expected_answer_elements: Keep FrameCandidate as the shared downstream unit and CandidateSource as a protocol exposing candidates(context) returning a list of FrameCandidate objects.
Represent an image collection with a mission-level CollectionContext whose ordered members include image_id, image_bytes, and ordinal, with image_ref only as an optional reserved field.
Decode each valid image to exactly one BGR ndarray using a function-local cv2 import so the output matches the video path.
Image candidates should not invent video timing values; temporal fields are nullable while image_id and ordinal preserve provenance.
A corrupt image is skipped and recorded as a per-item failure while other members continue; an empty member list returns an empty candidate list.
Do not add module-level heavy imports or modify pyproject.toml or uv.lock.

support: The UES1 conversation defines FrameCandidate and CandidateSource as the shared seam.
The UES2 conversation defines CollectionContext membership, one BGR candidate per image, nullable temporal fields, and per-item decode failures.
Both conversations require air-gap-safe imports and no dependency-lock changes.

rationale: The repository-specific contracts and BGR/provenance rules are not inferable from a generic image pipeline question and would otherwise require codebase rediscovery.
safety: Uses only generic project terminology and omits personal paths and sensitive domains.
